answer: A defense: correlate funding paths and invite edges across identities. One operator spinning up many masks tends to seed them from a single wallet or invite tree, a telltale ember of shared origin. The protocol clusters accounts by overlapping funding ancestors and shared invite links, then caps rewards per cluster, not per address. So a sybil swarm, however polished its sonnet-smooth answers, collapses to one earning unit. To truly split, an attacker must fund each identity from independently earned, disjoint balances and route invites through unrelated peers, so no mask finds a cheap haven.
